source.citation: Balonis, M. (2019). Thermodynamic modelling of temperature effects on the mineralogy of Portland cement systems containing chloride. Cement and Concrete Research 120, 66-76.
source.location: Section 2 and Table 1 (p. 67), Section 3 and the captions of Figs. 5, 6, 11 and 12 (pp. 69-74)

transcription.from: the published article (PDF): Table 1 from the text layer, checked against the rendered page; the compositions from the figure captions; the transition temperatures and the shrinkages as the text of Section 3 prints them
transcription.note: The article computes with GEMS-PSI, alkali- and CO2-free, the cement hydrates from its refs. 7, 10 and 30, Friedel's and Kuzel's salts from Table 1, ideal solid solutions of Friedel's salt with the hydroxy-AFm and with monocarbonate, and the SO4/OH-AFm and SO4/CO3-AFt solid solutions of its refs. 11, 23, 30 and 31; the activity coefficients by the Truesdell-Jones equation with b = 0.064 and Kielland's ion sizes (Eq. 5). The transition temperatures are calculated results the text states, most of them approximately ('around', '~'); they are transcribed as printed, with the wording.

c3a.description: Tricalcium aluminate of the model mixture.

portlandite.description: Portlandite of the model mixture, present at every temperature.

water.description: Water of the model mixture, 60 ml.

so3_al2o3.description: Molar SO3/Al2O3 ratio of every mixture, the sulfate as CaSO4.

calcite_with_carbonate.description: Calcite of the carbonate-bearing mixtures, CO2/Al2O3 = 0.75.

chloride_afm_thermodynamics.location: Table 1, p. 67: Friedel's salt C4ACl2H10 and Kuzel's salt C4As0.5ClH12 at 298 K

temperature_scans.location: Section 3 and the captions of Figs. 5, 6, 11 and 12: the fixed compositions computed from 0 to 99 C, 0.01 mol C3A, 0.015 mol portlandite and 60 ml water, SO3/Al2O3 = 1; the chloride as CaCl2, its ratio written 2Cl/Al2O3 (1 for Friedel's salt), the carbonate as calcite

rows: Kuzel's salt forms but is predicted to be stable only up to 28 C
SO4-AFmss starts to appear at around 28 C
Friedel's salt persists up to 80 C, above which it decomposes
CO3-AFm substituted with chloride is stable up to ~50 C
Friedel's salt (Cl-AFm) persists up to 70 C
Friedel's salt and ettringite persist up to ~90 C
Friedel's salt and ettringite persist up to ~90 C
above this temperature [70 C] volumetric shrinkage ... is estimated at around 15%
the associated shrinkage is estimated at the level of 23%
at 90 C system shrunk by around 30% as compared to 0 C
above 90 C shrinkage ... is estimated at 25% as compared to 0 C

notes: The figures (total volume of the solids against temperature) are not digitized; the comparison uses the transitions and shrinkages the text states.
Friedel's salt is written C4ACl2H10 in Table 1 and C4AClH10 in Cemdata18, the same formula, Ca4Al2Cl2(OH)12(H2O)4.
